description:
Reframed as a single unified 6-DATASET sweep (2026-09-26): TotalSeg CT itself is now measured through the exact same eval.py / fixed-3mm / single-level / fp32 / test-split protocol as the 5 held-out sources below, instead of being reported separately via train.py's internal bf16 epoch-250 val-split eval (that older in-distribution table in 1a_feature_fusion / 3_results.md used a DIFFERENT tool, precision, spacing (4.24mm), split (val), and a matched-epoch snapshot rather than each run's own best.pt -- not directly comparable to the numbers here). TotalSeg CT here uses dataset=d2_varspacing_15_6 (CT-only, v2 loader, crop_spacing_mm=3 is its own default, val_classes=all so seen/unseen tagging comes free via resolve_classes, eval.split=test -- 89 subjects, a genuinely held-out slice distinct from the val split used for checkpoint selection during training). Trade-off of unifying onto real best.pt checkpoints: exact epoch-matching across the three arms is lost (150 stopped ~epoch 263, 151 ~epoch 260, 152 fully converged at epoch ~399) -- a minor caveat for 150/151 (3 epochs apart) but material for 152, which had far more training left to give.

Original 5-source OOD sweep description (unchanged in scope, just no longer a separate protocol from TotalSeg CT): cold-transformer chain's three architecture arms (150=bi-axial, 151=single-axis fusion l=9, 152=medverse baseline -- see 1a_feature_fusion/runs.json for the superseded in-distribution comparison) across totalseg_mri (CT-trained models' first exposure to TotalSegmentator's own MRI-modality subjects -- these models saw data.source_mix.regime_p=[1,0,0], i.e. CT-only tasks during training despite the multisource_ct_mri dataset group nominally including MRI), hu_lwk1 (CT, L1 vertebra measurement ROI), msd_prostate (MRI T2+ADC, PZ/TZ zones), msd_hippocampus (MRI T1, ant/post), flare22 (CT, 13 abdominal organs). ALL SIX evaluated single-level (no cascade) at a FIXED data.crop_spacing_mm=3 (inside these checkpoints' own train_spacing_range=[3,6], deliberately uniform across sources rather than each source's own individually-tuned default spacing -- cross-source Dice differences reflect task difficulty at a held resolution, not each source's best-case setup; predictable consequence: small targets (msd_hippocampus, msd_prostate) score lower here than their own tuned-spacing numbers reported elsewhere). eval.split=test uniformly (a no-op for hu_lwk1/msd_prostate/msd_hippocampus/flare22 -- none of those providers implement train/val/test split filtering, every converted case is eval data; REQUIRED for totalseg_mri and totalseg, whose meta.csv splits are train/test and train/val/test respectively). eval.n_subjects=null (full coverage, no subsampling). fp32 eval (eval.autocast=false, the harness default) uniformly across all three models. This standalone eval.py run has no query_prior injection for any model (single-level eval never touches it), so this sweep has NO recipe asymmetry between the three arms -- the cleanest of the three-way comparisons run so far. Checkpoints are each run's best.pt as of 2026-09-26 (all three training runs had stopped; GPU idle, no active training process at sweep time).
